tom_tat: The translator Hanh Doan introduces the origins of the book and her heartfelt wish to share true stories of cause and effect so that readers will deeply believe in karma and live better, happier lives.
noi_dung:
Translator's Preface

This book is divided into three parts: the first by layman Guoqing; the second a collection of stories by many authors from many countries (who witnessed events with their own eyes or heard them told) and sent to the Chinese Ethical Society; the third written by a reporter from direct interviews or from hearsay.

I spared no effort hunting through the vast forest of memoirs in the original Chinese to find stories that are good and useful; then I distilled and selected them, and translated them to share with readers. You have every right to believe or not. But this volume is not mere reading "to buy a moment's idle amusement"; it carries the love for humanity of both its writers and its translator.

In these present days, open a newspaper or a website and we see crimes abounding — cruel and horrifying to an alarming degree. It all comes from people not believing in cause and effect. Because they do not believe, they know no fear, and so take no care to guard themselves. So much so that an education researcher had to lament: this is the age when "evil reigns supreme!"

There is a saying: "Sages fear the cause; ordinary beings fear the result." Why do sages fear the cause? Because they have witnessed much, have suffered, and have felt it to the very marrow, so they are always careful, guarding every act and thought. As for us, we witness little, understand little, believe little, remember little... so we lose all control and sow causes recklessly and at random. Take, for example, a cashier guarding a "vault of gold" for a company or a private employer: if he does not believe in the retribution of wrongdoing and blessing, he will very easily embezzle and greedily create offenses. But if he believes in cause and effect, understanding that "ill-gotten gains can not only never be enjoyed but will bring calamity upon oneself and one's descendants"... then even with no supervisor watching, he will keep himself pure and honest.

My only wish is that after reading this book you will see cause and effect more clearly, and live a better and happier life. If this work brings its readers even a little spiritual benefit, or joy in the meaning of life, that is the translator's greatest reward.

I would like to offer my gratitude to Hong Minh Chau, to Mrs. Nguyen Tam, and to the silent contributions of so many people who helped me in spirit and in substance so that I could complete this translation and offer it to readers, even though the gifted copies are limited and modest in number.

I dedicate this field of merit to all my benefactors, to my elder sister Nguyen Huy Phuong, to the spirit of my grandchild Carol Chi Phan,... and to all people living in this world. May you always be peaceful and happy, and may your wisdom and compassion ever shine so that together we build a beautiful human realm.

Finally, I beg your forgiveness for the translator's errors.

Hanh Doan, 29/03/2013

COMMENTARY:
The translator's preface skillfully lays the foundation for the whole book: cause and effect is not some distant matter after death, but is present in every thought, word, and deed each day. The translator stresses that "sages fear the cause, ordinary beings fear the result" — the wise take care over every cause they sow, while the deluded are terrified only when retribution arrives. This book does not aim to threaten with fear, but to awaken a deep faith in the law of cause and effect so that each person willingly lives virtuously, carefully, and accumulates blessings. That is the most precious gift the translator wishes to entrust to us.

tom_tat: Cư sĩ Quả Khanh kể lại hành trình từ người theo chủ nghĩa vô thần đến quy y Phật pháp sau chuyến du ngoạn núi Ngũ Đài Sơn, gặp gỡ lão Hòa thượng, và tâm nguyện ghi chép những câu chuyện nhân quả có thật để chia sẻ với độc giả.
noi_dung:
Author's words

The reason I came to religion

I was born in 1944, and because I received an atheist education from a young age, I always considered religion to be superstition.So how did I enter the path of studying Buddhism?The story originates from a trip to Ngu Dai Son mountain in the summer more than ten years ago.

Mount Wutai in Shanxi Province is one of the four renowned sacred mountains of Chinese Buddhism, revered as the bodhimaṇḍa of Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. On the mountain there are magnificent, solemn and famous thousand-year-old pagodas that I have walked through.In Dai Hung Bao Dien, there is always the smoke of incense, even the humming of Dai Hong Chung makes the listener feel lightheaded and exhausted.The scenery here always gives me an indescribable feeling of excitement, as if I have known this place for a long time.

The second time I went to Wutai Mountain to visit, I was very excited and suddenly came up with the idea to learn about the peaceful retreat of the ascetic monks, because few people knew about their activities.I always remember that morning, the air was cold and the fog was thick.With an eager heart, I packed my gear, carefully brought a map, and embarked alone on a journey to explore the secluded scenic landscape. I did not expect that that very adventure would change my life and that of many others in the future.Until now, I have always considered Wutai Mountain as the land of my second birth.

When starting out, I deliberately avoided flat roads and only chose winding paths to go.Along the way, looking up, we only see towering mountain peaks, dark trees, swirling smoke and fog, and sparkling snow.I feel refreshed and my mind is empty.The road becomes more and more bumpy.I kept walking along the stream, admiring the "old wood and cold rock" picture of nature; Cold rocks, tall old trees, luxuriant vegetation; The sky is blue, the clouds are white, the road is full of strange herbs and flowers.I was attracted by the external environment, drunk forever, forgetting everything in life and immersed in the beautiful blue water scene.

I was so engrossed in climbing the pass and wading through the stream that I forgot that it was almost noon, but by that time I still hadn't seen the silhouette of any ascetic monk, and I couldn't help but feel a little disappointed.While I was looking around in a confused mood, I suddenly heard the sound of a gong coming from far away: "Knock!Glass!Glass!"The ancient echoes seemed to be hidden somewhere, hovering in the mountains, the resounding sound came from the mountain valley, in the dark forest to the west.

My spirit was uplifted again, I struggled to move towards the mountain valley.Turning onto a deep but beautiful road, high above was covered with purple clouds, and the green trees were like a fairyland.At this time, the sound of the gong gradually slowed down and then stopped completely.A meandering stream of clear blue water appeared before me, spraying out steam like pearls.I bent down to grab some water to drink, the cool and refreshing taste made my mouth smell good.After drinking enough, I washed my face and used my hand to splash water on my face.Suddenly I noticed someone standing by the stream so I raised my head.

An old monk with unshaven hair and beard, his shirt patched with grass, was standing there with his arms folded.The wind blew past, his beard and hair moved, his shirt fluttered, our four eyes met for a moment but I felt dizzy, my mind was confused.How pure and gentle the monk's eyes are.I felt like he was so familiar, as if he were my parents from a previous life. He radiated a strong charisma that confused my mind and body...

– Donor, sorry to bother you!– The monk clasped his hands and said.
- No!It was me who disturbed a pure cultivator like you - I responded in bewilderment
– Does the donor like this quiet area?
– Yes, I just wanted to avoid the hustle and bustle a bit so I went for a walk alone to see the scenery.(Actually, I didn't mean what I said, because I was secretly wishing for a moment of enlightenment like this!)

– Well, after all, it's disturbing the donor, the donor can just walk around, the monk will go first!

Before I could stop being surprised, the Venerable had already gently glided towards the West.I quickly chased after him and shyly confessed:
– Venerable monk, please stop, I am actually looking forward to meeting a high monk like you...

– How good!I'm not a "high monk", I'm just a monk leading the way in the countryside.

– Was it you who knocked the bell just now?– I asked
The Venerable replied leisurely
– The sound of the gong awakens the hearts of the guests
The clear blue water cleanses the dirty mind

I silently contemplated what the Venerable had just said, and in a moment I followed him to a beautiful, clear area, surrounded by many pear trees.The root is very large, the fruit is lush.The terrain in the north is slightly higher, and in front there is a small hermitage.In my heart, I happily thought to myself: "I have met a noble monk who has transcended the world."

- We and the world should not stay hidden for long, time is limited, don't wait until death to practice.Fame and fortune are just nothing, love in this world will eventually pass away, injustice and retribution will always continue without end...

The monk pretended to be humming unintentionally, but when he heard it, my heart was secretly shocked.

- People in this world only know how to create injustice, do not know how to repent, only know how to enjoy happiness but do not accumulate blessings.Little do they know: reciting the Buddha's name once increases immeasurable blessings; bowing before the Buddha once eradicates offenses as numerous as the sands of the Ganges!

Hearing that, I could no longer control myself, so I took two steps forward and knelt down in front of the old monk, earnestly saying:
"Master, I pray that you will accept me as your disciple; I wish to learn the Buddha Dharma from you."

"The Buddha Dharma is like an ocean; only through faith can one enter. Do you truly have 'faith'?"
The monk deliberately emphasized the word "believe"

This question left me speechless.Alas!All my life, I had always regarded Buddhism as superstition, holding a dismissive attitude and giving no heed to bowing before Buddhas and Bodhisattvas... Today I don't understand why I sincerely kneel at the feet of a monk I've never known, begging to become a disciple like this?

For a moment, it was difficult for me to respond.But "no, quit, repent"...These words kept echoing and continuously imprinted in my brain, shaking my mind. A great feeling suddenly arose in my heart as if it had been there for a long time.

While I was confused and my spirit was without a master, I suddenly saw the old monk looking at me compassionately and attentively. In that moment, my mind had hundreds of thousands of mixed emotions, each drop of tears kept flowing, falling down and wetting the old monk's pure white socks.Though feeling exceedingly rude and awkward, I could not stem the torrent of tears streaming down, like an errant child who had made a grave mistake, unable to speak, doing nothing but weeping and weeping.

– Faith is the mother of all merits, the source of religion.But faith is divided into "true faith" and "superstition".It is called "right faith", meaning right and not wrong, enlightened but not delusional.People who take refuge in Buddhism first need to establish accurate views."One bows to the Buddha out of reverence for the Buddha’s virtue; one recites the Buddha’s name in gratitude for the Buddha; one reads sutras to understand the principles; one sits in meditation to realize the Buddha’s state of mind. The enlightened person attains the Buddha's way..."

I was like a hungry person who was fed, thirsty was given a drink, listening to every word, every word revealing His pearls, feeling like every blade of grass, every tree in front of me was radiating a brilliant golden light, I kept listening respectfully without knowing that the sun had fallen to the West.

When he saw me leave, the Venerable took a pear from a rock hole in the stream and gave it to me.At that time I had not eaten breakfast or lunch.I thanked Him and brought the pear to my mouth to bite. The cold, fragrant flavor cooled my teeth. It felt like my lungs were clearing and my heart was refreshed. I was surprised because I felt like I had just eaten a fairy fruit.The monk looked at me eating deliciously, his compassionate face smiled slightly, his deep smile of joy touched my heart, making me feel like we had known each other and been close for a long time.

– This pear originally had a bitter taste and was difficult to swallow, but it was soaked in sweet spring water for three months, so it turned sweet.This stream has a cool winter and cool summer. Pears can be stored in the water all year round.

– That being said, can you stay here all year round to practice?– I asked curiously.The monk smiled and did not deny it.

“The ancient moon is like dew, the clear wind is like water”…The small stream gurgled.The Venerable and I walked and talked on the way home.Before I felt cold or tired, I reached the rough road outside.I clasped my hands and bowed to the Venerable.My heart overflows with attachment and does not want to leave Him...But I know it's useless to talk too much.

As if understanding my feelings, the Venerable spoke softly.
– "If you are destined to meet someone, you will meet them."

His appearance is like an "ancient moon" disappearing into the forest.What I feel comforted is that the monk said earlier that he would soon end the retreat and begin "entering the world to save people, preaching the Dharma depending on the situation."Thinking about this fills my heart with joy.I walked faster on the way home and had the feeling that if I sped up my legs, I would soon see Him a little faster.

Returning to the hall, I sat quietly in the living room, recalling the dream-like meeting I had just had, secretly feeling extremely interesting.Suddenly I remembered that I had not asked the Venerable's name, and my sadness and regret were inconsolable.I always hope to soon enjoy His blessings.

Not long after, I contacted the Venerable.Since then, we have had a deep relationship, and I have always been close to Him.

The light and sound permeated, more than ten years passed in a flash.Now, at the age of nearly 60, during this period I see the Venerable devote all his heart to the Dharma, forgetting himself and educating countless sentient beings.As for myself, I have lived my days in vain; unable to completely let go, it has been difficult to attain true benefit—how deeply shameful!

However, right now I don't want to destroy these flexible, meaningful stories, and don't want these real and extremely valuable cause-and-effect lessons to be buried deep in the grave.Therefore, after hesitation and long consideration, I picked up my pen and recorded these true stories to share with readers.

If I do not clearly state the names and locations related to the real characters mentioned in the book, it is because I consider it inconvenient.Hope you understand.

In addition, it is possible that some of the words used in the book are no longer suitable today due to old place names and names remaining.I just hope that Venerable Venerables and Dharma friends in the religion will kindly help me correct this.

May everyone grow in discipline, concentration, and wisdom, cultivate both blessings and insight, and swiftly attain the Buddha path.

COMMENTS:
The Author's Words is a moving account of transformation from an atheist who disdained religion into a devout Buddhist after receiving guidance from the venerable elder on Mount Wutai. The image of a bitter pear soaked in spring water for three months and becoming sweet is a profound metaphor: even if the mind is initially dry and confused, if one meets a good friend and practices persistently, it can be transformed into the sweetness of enlightenment.Layman Qua Khanh used his own life experience to prove that "If you have fate, you will meet", and recording these stories of cause and effect is his way of repaying his teacher and benefiting sentient beings.

tom_tat: The story is about a disobedient, unfilial young Taiwanese man who became a gangster, beat his parents leading to their death, and later suffered from an incurable disease.Met Venerable Dieu Phap at Ngu Dai Mountain, was reprimanded, repented, took refuge, and recovered.

The story of Truong Nghia, 24 years old, suffered from ankylosing spondylitis due to eating too many frogs, fish, and eels.Gặp Hòa thượng Diệu Pháp, được chỉ rõ nguyên nhân nhân quả, ăn chay niệm Phật sám hối và khỏi bệnh.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**SHOCKED UP**}

My name is Truong Nghia, I live in Thien Tan city, I am 24 years old this year.At the age of 19, I became seriously ill. At first I lost feeling in my legs and had difficulty walking. That night my illness got worse. My hips and joints were unbearably painful and my legs couldn't move. Every time I squeezed them, the pain made my whole body convulse.

The doctor finished examining him and said:
– This disease is extremely rare, cannot be diagnosed, and can only be temporarily called "spondylitis".This disease cannot be cured, you can only go home to rest.

When I got home, I lay in bed all day, and at night the pain was even more intense, and I couldn't sleep.During the day, my parents went everywhere to ask doctors for diagnosis and treatment. At night, they witnessed me moaning in pain, my heart aching like hell, and I couldn't sleep.In just a few days, my parents' bodies were already emaciated, weak, and very old.

My mother had a colleague named Yang who studied Buddhism in his youth and understood the teachings deeply. Mr. Duong took refuge under the Venerable Dieu Phap at Ngu Dai Mountain, diligently practiced Precepts, concentration, wisdom, and propagated the Dharma to save people.In this situation where I had an incurable disease like this, I heard Layman Duong say that Venerable Dieu Phap had a very deep understanding of cause and effect. Anyone who had an incurable disease that was difficult to cure and came to him would be freed from a long-term, tormenting illness.All were not treated but healed and recovered just like dying and coming back to life.

Hearing this, my parents became even more impatient and quickly went to see Venerable Dieu Phap to see what was going on.

When my grandparents finished telling him about my illness, the Venerable asked:
– Does your son really like to eat frog meat?
My mother replied:
– Yes, yes!He loves stir-fried frog with chili, eating it two or three times a week.

The Venerable said again:
– Right now your legs are shaped like the word "bow", right?As he spoke, he used his hands to sketch and describe.
– Yes, its legs have the same shape – my mother replied

The Venerable continued to ask:
– Do you see that shape like a frog?
Seeing my parents bewildered, He said:
– I got this disease because I ate too many frogs and got a cold.This is what the Buddhists often say is "Cause and effect retribution".

He then explained Buddhist principles, clearly speaking about cause and effect and retribution, and presented real evidence.Moreover, the Venerable Master also personally came to my house to check on me. First, he encouraged me to be resilient in facing my illness. Next, he told me to do exactly as he taught and my illness would definitely go away.The Venerable revealed the theory of cause and effect and retribution, explaining the six realms of reincarnation, making me extremely moved and feeling like I was walking in a dark night and suddenly a light illuminated me. I felt that only He could save me.

The monk was teaching the Dharma while trying to massage my feet with his hands.Seeing that, my mother hurriedly stopped her:
– Please don't do that, because every time I touch it, my child will cringe in pain and tremble all over

The monk smiled and told me:
– So should I massage the baby again?

Because I was afraid of pain, I was very afraid of people touching me, but because I had very deep trust in the Venerable, I agreed.Strangely enough, when the Venerable Master's hands touched my legs, not only did I not feel any pain, but I also felt warm, relaxed, and extremely comfortable.A while ago, my parents and I were worried and worried, but now I feel at ease. I'm so grateful that tears flow freely.If my legs can recover healthily, this will be a lifetime of happiness and luck.My heart is filled with faith and admiration for the Venerable.Once again, He has rekindled my optimism and joy in life.The monk also told me that from now on I should not eat frogs anymore, nor should I kill animals to eat them. If possible, I should become a vegetarian to help my body recover quickly.

He explained, "Great sins fill the sky, repentance will immediately disappear."As long as I sincerely repented and confessed the killing karma I created, diligently reciting the Buddha's name daily to dedicate merits to all the living beings I harmed, my legs would gradually recover.

I obeyed his words, beginning to eat vegetarian food and recite the Buddha's name. My parents also recited Buddha's name for support, praying for me to get well soon.And my illness gradually changed for the better.

But when my friends came to visit and saw that my body was too weak, they all advised me to eat meat and fish for nutrients.My parents were also impatient and told me to wait until my body was completely healthy before becoming a vegetarian.Due to my unstable faith, I was persuaded by everyone, so I went back to eating fish and meat.Later, when chanting the Ksitigarbha Sutra, I realized that I was the type of person who "had just developed a kind heart, but in a moment quickly retreated."

As a result, after I ate salty food again, my legs started to hurt intensely again.No matter what injections or medicine I took, it was all ineffective.At this time, my parents frantically went to find Venerable Dieu Phap, but layperson Duong said that the Venerable had gone to Nam Phuong Tu to preach the Dharma.

Through many difficulties and hardships, we finally contacted Him.

Over the phone, the Venerable asked:
– You eat fish and eels again, right?

Feeling hot like fire, my mother intervened and said:
– Yes, that's right, fish and eels can help your child nourish his blood and strengthen his body...

The monk sighed and said:
– Oh my!Why don't you remember what I told you, eating fish and meat does not benefit the body, it only harms and increases sins, making the illness worse!It's true that old karma hasn't been eliminated yet, but it causes new karma!Last time I showed you how to recuperate. If you perseveringly practice vegetarianism, Buddha-recitation, sincere repentance, and vow to abstain from evil, your condition would certainly improve, rather than worsening like this.

After hearing this, the whole family regretted it.We expressed our repentance and earnestly promised to obey the Venerable this time.Then, let's ask Him to teach us how to save.The monk told me to recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra and the Great Compassion Mantra, to sincerely repent, and thus gradually eliminate karma.The monk forced me to chant diligently every day, dedicating the merit of reciting mantras to sentient beings throughout the dharma realm, so that the effect would be good.

From that day on, I really began to learn and practice Buddhism.Every day, earnestly recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra and the Great Compassion Mantra.There are many words I don't know.So I had to buy a recorder to chant along. I persevered and didn't dare to be lazy.Before long I was able to recite the Great Compassion Mantra by heart.And finished reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra within two hours.I think it is thanks to the blessings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas that it can have such quick results.My parents also received immeasurable comfort because of my sincerity in studying Buddhism and practicing Dharma.

Every day I focused my mind on sutra chanting, mantra recitation, and mindfulness of the Buddha, dedicating myself to cultivation. Even if others advised me to eat meat, I would not be moved.Thanks to that, the disease gets better and better.Then I went to the hospital for a follow-up examination.The doctor diagnosed that the femur was necrotic.I also combine treatment with Oriental medicine, my disease is a rare incurable complication.But my miracle gradually appeared: I could walk without pain, I thought: "This is the scene that changes according to the mind."

Since it is karmic retribution, one should not fear, lament, or weep; one need only face it calmly, maintain deep faith in the Buddha Dharma, and practice with wholehearted devotion, which will surely transform adverse circumstances into wholesome ones. Through this experience, I hope that those who watch my story will take it as an example and be careful and vigilant. I hope you will stop killing, so as not to fall into the same mistake as me.Because if I hadn't personally gone through this painful and memorable experience, it would be difficult for me to believe in the theory of karma and retribution, about the crime of killing!It is true that the cause and effect of retribution is very clear, like a shadow following the shape, without any deviation.

Therefore, I hope you will soon wake up, understand that killing will surely result in evil consequences, and stop eating salty food.Please look at my story, after receiving evil retribution, I realized how to awaken, thanks to that I developed more wisdom and had more blessings.I always remember the saying: "Evil is rewarded with evil, good is rewarded with good."

Whatever we do, every action, every thought, has consequences.People who have practiced and attained enlightenment can immediately know the cause at a glance. Otherwise, how could Venerable Dieu Phap clearly understand that the cause of my illness was caused by eating frogs, fish, eels...Which way should you feel?Please think carefully.

COMMENTS:
Truong Nghia's story SHOCKED Awakening is a bloody lesson about "Eating the flesh of living beings - suffering retribution on the body".His fondness for eating frogs, fish, and eels directly caused him to contract ankylosing spondylitis, causing his legs to curl up like a frog.When you persistently fast, recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra and dedicate the Great Compassion Mantra to sentient beings who have been harmed, your illness will immediately improve.But when the ventricle rots and eats salty food again, the disease recurs immediately.This proves that cause and effect retribution is as quick and clear as a shadow following a picture.The story also emphasizes the importance of "steadfast faith" - not letting others sway, and the merit of repenting and killing karma by chanting dedication sutras.This is a warning for those who still underestimate the karma of killing: "One bite of food, one bite of sin."If you want to be healthy, stop killing."

tom_tat: Mr. Chuong has terminal lung cancer due to killing many chickens, especially the majestic yellow-feathered rooster.His wife repented, chanted Ksitigarbha sutra for the chicken and he miraculously recovered from his illness.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**YELLOW-FEATURED ROOT**}

There was a farmer named Chuong whose lung cancer reached a stage where both major hospitals declared that they had given up and told his family to prepare for his funeral.

A relative of his who knew I studied Buddhist principles brought Mr. Zhang's wife to my home, asking for assistance. Fortunately, Venerable Dieu Phap was present there, and they immediately begged Master to mercifully help them.

Venerable Dieu Phap said:
– The patient's killing karma is too heavy, especially killing a lot of chickens, is that true?
Mr. Chuong's wife replied:
– Yes, my husband and I like fried, stewed, grilled...In the village, if there is a wedding, celebration or funeral, they always come to ask him to be the head chef.In addition, he criticized the chicken killer for not being good at techniques, so he always took action.Every time he held a party, he killed dozens of chickens, the red blood dyed the whole ditch pink.

The Venerable asked again:
– Have you secretly killed any other person's big rooster?This chicken's belly is all yellow, its body is pink-brown, it has a dark green tail, its whole body is sparkling, when it looks up - the height from head to toe - is more than half a meter, it looks very majestic and majestic...

When Ms. Chuong heard the Venerable describe it, she was startled, her face lost color, and she fell down with a thud.She shook her head repeatedly and stammered:
– Oh my God, Bodhisattva!…Who do we know…kill chickens…is guilty?
That year there was a bad harvest, the family was hungry every day!That day, a neighbor's big rooster flew to our house.It is true that we secretly killed it and ate it, but we did not expect that Bodhisattva had eyes that could see through everything.This is called "evil meets evil." In the future, we will not dare to arbitrarily appropriate other people's property.During that famine year, we also stole more food from the state to eat, and even stole crops...Now I know my crime, it was all my husband's reckless doing, please shorten my lifespan!I would like to die for him...Huhuhuhu!

The wife was very mentally shaken. She cried and told the story for a while, constantly asking to repent for her sins, making the listener deeply moved.Who would have thought that this woman had a very high intuition and could understand everything with just a little talk.Her words were honest and simple, but their love as husband and wife was also very precious.

I quickly helped her up and told her to listen to the Venerable's explanation.

Master is also very touched.He said in a slightly trembling voice:
– Your recent crying shows that you are very sincere and repentant.When you return, remember to explain to your husband and children, so that he knows his mistake and urgently repent.From now on, both of you absolutely must not kill anymore.Go to the temple to get the Ksitigarbha sutra. Because your husband and children kill a lot of chickens, you have to recite it 49 times to dedicate it to them.Remember that your husband must diligently recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra. He also committed the crime of stealing and killing that big rooster, which is the king of chickens!

And the Venerable continued to ask:
– Is it true that after killing that 'mighty' rooster, my husband and I immediately got a headache?
Ms. Chuong thought about it and then affirmed:
– Yes, that's right!Indeed, at that time he was sick with a headache for about two days, he was in pain, and couldn't eat anything!

The Venerable said:
– After the chicken was killed, it always followed the newspaper and stood on her husband's head, sometimes even using its beak to peck at his brain.So how can it not be painful?Please set up a tablet for that chicken in the temple. You two must recite the 7 Ksitigarbha Sutras for it and invite the monks to help it achieve its salvation.It can transcend heaven into a phoenix!

Ms. Chuong said:
– We don't know many words and can't recite, so what should we do?

– Chanting is to save the lives of your husband and children!In addition, it also has great benefits for children.If you are not literate, you can look it up in the dictionary, you can also ask someone who is literate. If you cannot recite it, you can ask a monk to recite it, but it is not as good as reciting it yourself, because this merit is all yours to make.Be absolutely careful, during the transition period, you should cut off all salty foods, all things like meat, onions, chives, garlic, alcohol and smoking...Everything must end.

Because if you eat foul-smelling food and then recite the sutras, no gods or ghosts will come to listen to the sutras, and sentient beings will not benefit.But that is not respectful towards Buddhism.So how can we gain merit?If the animals are killed, if they do not get better, their husband's and children's illnesses will be very difficult to heal.If both of you strictly observe the precepts, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will surely bestow their protection and blessings upon you.

The Venerable reminded him earnestly.Ms. Chuong asked again:
– My husband is currently critically ill. I don't know when he will die. Will I have time to chant this sutra?

The Venerable replied:
– If my husband hadn't killed so many chickens, his life would not have ended.Killing is shortening life!Because I recently revealed my repentance from the bottom of my heart, now my husband's illness also has a chance to change.Be sincere in repentance and help your husband eliminate his sins.If your husband himself sincerely repents and earnestly recites sutras and the Buddha's name, danger will surely turn into safety. We must take advantage of the remaining opportunities!

Mrs. Chuong immediately went to the hospital and saw that her husband was able to sit up and was sitting on the bed.Upon asking, he found out that he had just vomited more than two and a half cups of pus into the spittoon.Breathing has also cleared.This is the first time since he was seriously ill that he was able to vomit phlegm.Mrs. Chuong was extremely happy and took the opportunity to bring the Venerable's teachings to her husband.After hearing the story, her husband was both happy and scared.

The next day, both decided to go home from the hospital. They told the hospital:
– Anyway, we are out of medicine.

Then the couple did as the Venerable taught.Not long after, Mr. Chuong, who had "almost died from lung cancer", walked out of death's door to the surprise of the entire Village.Not only that, he can also ride a bicycle, which is a topic for the entire Village to inquire about and discuss.

Then, a heavy rain poured down and caused a leak in his house.He immediately climbed onto the roof to fix the leak, surprising the villagers, almost rubbing it forever.

COMMENTS:
The story of THE YELLOW-FEATURED ROOT clearly shows that "Killing animals - especially killing many chickens - attracts lung cancer".Mr. Chuong not only killed chickens en masse, but also secretly killed the majestic yellow-feathered rooster (the king of chickens), causing retribution to come quickly and severely.His wife, with sincere repentance, bowed her head and begged, revealed on her husband's behalf and vowed to recite sutras for salvation.As a result, Mr. Chuong miraculously recovered from his illness and was able to ride a bicycle and renovate his house.The story emphasizes: The karma of killing not only affects yourself but also your family; and the merit of repenting and reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra to dedicate to harmed sentient beings can turn danger into peace.This is a reminder for those who work as cooks, butchers or like to eat chicken: "Every chicken that is killed has resentment, sooner or later it will have to be repaid."

tom_tat: Mr. Jia had scabies all over his body due to adultery, raping many women, betraying his wife and being unfilial.Meeting Venerable Dieu Phap, his sins were exposed, he repented and recovered.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**"GOD GIVED" DISEASE**}

In early 1994, Mr. Gia, Ms. Ly's husband, got scabies.His whole body was covered with scabies, pus oozing and painful pain. He tried everywhere from Eastern to Western medicine but saw no results.

Ms. Ly called me and offered to take her husband to see Venerable Dieu Phap, but she was afraid that her husband was covered in scabies and the blood and pus smelled very inconveniently, so she was confused and hesitant, not knowing what to do.

Unexpectedly, 3 days later, she called again and happily informed me that her husband's ulcers had dried up in just one night and stopped draining pus.This was an incredibly strange thing ever since her husband got sick, so she was very excited and decided to take her husband to visit Master.

That evening, Ms. Ly and her husband arrived.Her husband is one meter eight meters tall, has a well-proportioned body, has a handsome and handsome appearance, and seems to be a talented person.As soon as the couple entered the door, they turned to Venerable Dieu Phap to pray, begging him for compassionate help.

As soon as she sat down, Ms. Ly asked Master:
– In just one night, my husband's scabies stopped flowing. Now there are no sores on his body. His illness has improved a lot. How is this happening?Please advise, Your Majesty.

The Venerable asked:
– Have you ever gone to the temple to pray to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva?
She replied:
– Yes, half a year ago, because I saw that his illness could not be cured, I often went to the temple to worship Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, asking Him to help my husband's illness heal quickly.

Master slowly said:
- You were able to come here today because you persistently worshiped Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and have now received inspiration.I must make it clear: while your deep virtuous roots and affinity with the Buddha brought you here, your husband's ailment is his own karmic retribution for wrongdoing. Only if he recognizes his faults, sincerely repents, and vows never to repeat them, will he fully recover. The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas always hope that wrongdoers will reform and turn toward the righteous path.

Master then turned to Ms. Ly's husband and asked:
– Do you think what I said is correct?
Mr. Gia nodded vigorously and replied:
– Yes!Yes!Teacher is right.

The Venerable continued:
– Because people do not understand the Dharma, they continually commit mistakes and even perpetrate evil. If you sincerely repent for the evil things you have done in the past, perhaps your illness will heal.

But Mr. Gia said clearly:
– I am a man of integrity; I have never harmed anyone, nor have I ever fought, scolded, or caused strife.

Seeing that, Master had to whisper and invite Ms. Ly out, then He asked again:
- Please, Mr. Gia, please check yourself to see if you have done anything bad in your life?

But Mr. Jia still insisted that he had "never done anything bad", his face remained calm, and he also told Master that if he knew, he would tell him.

The monk sighed and said:
– You're so seriously ill and you're still so confused!Look at how your wife sincerely worships and prays for Buddha's blessings for you!Now I ask you something - Master's voice became stern - When you were 20 years old, did you make friends with a girl a little shorter than you, with an oval face, white skin, and two pigtails?

Seeing that Mr. Jia seemed surprised, Master added:
– She often wears a shirt with white flowers that you gave her, is this okay?

No matter how calm and proud he was just now, Mr. Jia's face was pale, his eyes were terrified as he stared at the Venerable, he stammered:
- She…are classmates who follow their children from urban to rural areas, living in the same household.Why do You know her?

– So tell me, what is the relationship between the two sides?
– Yes, just a little fleeting love from youth...

– Is that so?I don't think it's that simple, because you used tricks to deceive and rape her, and in the end abandoned her, right?– Master asked sternly.

Mr. Jia was so shocked that he trembled. He quickly knelt down at Master's feet and whispered nervously:
– Master, please don't let my wife know that I really love that girl, then...

- After that, there were a few more girls who were also seduced by you...Even after getting married, before you got sick, you were still cheating on someone else's wife, right?– The monk said sternly, looking harsh.

At this time, all of Mr. Jia's evil deeds over the years were exposed without missing a beat.Just moments before he had spoken proudly claiming to be a gentleman of honor; now his expression was like a criminal's, trembling all over as he prostrated before the Master, kowtowing repeatedly and pleading for forgiveness.

– Master…I'm guilty!I won't dare do that again...

Witnessing this scene, my heart was deeply shaken: truly, 'the net of heaven is vast and wide, though meshes are coarse, nothing slips through.' Even though his crime of adultery was not punished by the law, his heart was trembling right now as if he was being sentenced to death, and his whole body seemed soulless.

The majestic master looked exactly like a judge, loudly commanding:
– First stand up and sit down. You not only engaged in illicit lust with others' wives and daughters, but deceived your parents, betrayed your wife, acted disloyally and unfilially—you are a true scoundrel! You committed every evil of lust without knowing how to reform and correct your ways. Soon your whole body will suffer from painful ulcers and die.If you die, you will certainly fall into hell!

Mr. Jia once again knelt down, passionately bowed his head to the Master, bowed, and promised that from now on he would not dare to do bad things again.He wept aloud, begging the Master to accept him as a disciple, vowing from then on to reform, cleanse his mind, and become a genuine Buddhist. Master nodded slightly, indicating acceptance.Then he called someone to invite Ms. Ly back in.The Master taught the couple the five precepts and ten virtues, and taught them how to repent and eliminate karma.They listened respectfully, until the sun fell to the west, then said goodbye and left, embracing the dharma in abundance.

After meeting Venerable Dieu Phap, the couple sincerely chanted sutras every day. Not long after, Mr. Jia recovered from his illness.Paying homage to the Buddha and chanting sutras became their daily practice. Husband and wife were of one heart and virtue, becoming a devout Buddhist family.

COMMENTS:
The story "GOD-GIVED" DISEASE is a profound lesson about "Lust - the retribution of scabies all over the body".Although Mr. Jia appeared virtuous and claimed to be "righteous", he raped many women, betrayed his wife, and was unfilial to his parents.The present retribution is ulcers all over the body, blood and pus stinking.When Venerable Dieu Phap exposed every detail of his sins (including the white floral shirt he gave to his lover), he trembled and sincerely repented.As a result, the illness was cured and the couple became devout Buddhists.The story reminds: "The sky's net is so thick that it is difficult to escape even a feather."Although earthly laws cannot punish the crime of lust, the law of cause and effect is never overlooked.People with families, wives and children, should know how to maintain chastity and filial piety to avoid tragic consequences like Mr. Jia.

tieu_de: 07. WHATEVER IS IN THE FACTORY, MY HOUSE HAS IT
tom_tat: Mr. Hong, a mechanic in a mechanical workshop, suffered from severe back pain due to the theft of national assets (iron, nails, screws...)bring it home.Met Venerable Dieu Phap, repented, paid back by making contributions, and recovered from his illness.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**WHAT IS IN THE WORKSHOP, MY HOUSE HAS THAT**}

Mr. Hong is over 50 years old and is a mechanic working in a government mechanical workshop.One afternoon he went with an old layman to visit Master Dieu Phap.As soon as he entered the door, he laughed loudly, clasped his hands, bowed respectfully three times before the Master, and without waiting to be invited to sit, he naturally sat down.At first glance, you can tell that his personality is very cheerful.

Master Dieu Phap asked him:
– Isn't it because you have back pain that you came here?
He was a little surprised and said:
– Master, you really have supernatural powers, I didn't say you already knew.After speaking, he stood up, lifted his shirt and exposed his back:
– Master, look, the belt is protecting my back.
All I could see was that the belt he was wearing was a loop of made-up tires, about 15cm wide.He sat down and continued:
– I've been wearing a back protector for nearly 10 years now. The doctor said my back muscles are damaged, and taking medication and injections is ineffective. I can only rely on this homemade belt. Without it to protect me, it's difficult for my back to stay straight!It's all because of working too hard when I was a child...

Pausing for a moment he continued:
– Listen to my friend say, You are a living Bodhisattva, please save me.He healed my back, and every day I will burn incense and worship Him, even if I have to make hundreds of prostrations every day, I will do it all - Having finished speaking, he clasped his hands and bowed to the Master again.

Venerable Dieu Phap smiled and said:
– First, I am not a Bodhisattva.Second, I am not a healer.If I were a Bodhisattva, could we still sit here and talk to each other?– If I could treat the disease, I would have to go to the hospital to do diagnosis.In fact, whether your illness is good or not, the right to decide is up to you.Because, removing the bell must be done by the person tying it.Now, I ask you, if I told you not to smoke, not drink alcohol, not steal, not eat salty foods, would you be able to do it?

– As long as I am sick, I can be cured. I will do whatever I ask you to keep, but I am not a thief or a thief!

– In addition to feeling pain in your back, sometimes you also feel a lot of pressure?
– Yes, that's right, it's like there are dozens of kilograms weighing on my back.

– He took things from the factory such as: iron, hinges, nails, screws, etc., what not?Maybe bring the whole trunk home?
When Mr. Hong heard that, he sat stunned, then nodded and said:
– This is indeed the case!Because you are a worker in a factory, "you will be rewarded with the moon on the front porch", in this day and age, who wouldn't take some of the nation's belongings as their own?Is that what you call stealing?Even our factory manager took things home, right?– Mr. Hong explained and argued.

– Bringing national treasure home as your own, if not theft then what is it?So you honestly take the things and bring them home?Or sneak things into the empty rice bowl, then keep wandering eyes...take it out of the factory.Is that so?– The monk seriously questioned.

Master's question stunned Mr. Hong.He opened his eyes wide and looked at the Venerable, speechless.

The Venerable continued
- Not only that, he also took pliers, screwdrivers, steel wire, and took iron and steel from the workshop to make household items such as: chimneys, garbage disposals, stoves, chopsticks, tongs...

Mr. Hong suddenly interrupted the Venerable:
– Master, how do you know?

– They are pressing on your back, making it impossible for you to stand straight!

Suddenly I felt that the study room had become like an interrogation room. Mr. Hong's fiery enthusiasm when entering the room earlier had turned into sadness and sadness. He struggled pitifully and said in a low voice:
– The items I brought back were absolutely not for my own use, nor did I sell them, most of them were given to my friends and neighbors.Because workers have low wages, they still take public goods from the state anyway, even warehouse keepers do the same.This was originally a matter of sympathy and mutual support, an "unspoken" thing in the factory, but I didn't know it was theft.Just now, Master said, I heard it like lightning exploding in the clear sky, causing my mind to be shaken and awakened.Truly the sky has eyes!You know everything I secretly stole from you.Moreover, all of that is now on my back.This is truly "retribution for evil and evil".Over the years, my illness has gotten worse and worse, and it turns out that the things I've secretly taken have become more and more.Today I understand clearly: "If you want others not to know, then don't do it yourself."This sentence is so true!I promise you, Master: starting from now, I firmly resolve to strictly observe your conditions—no smoking, no alcohol, no meat, no stealing state property. Tomorrow I will invite a Buddha statue home to venerate. I deeply regret that I came to believe in the Buddha Dharma so late. Otherwise I wouldn't have done bad things.I would like to ask you, which Buddhist book should I recite?

I truly did not expect Mr. Hong to possess such deep awakening; hearing him express his heartfelt repentance repentance, my heart was filled with Dharma joy. Seeing that Master was also happy, I immediately said:
– I will give you some Buddhist books for you to read first, then you can go to the temple to get Buddhist scriptures to read.

Mr. Hong thanked me and then turned back to ask the Venerable:
– Can the things I took from the factory be brought back now? Can they be converted into money and returned?

The Venerable said:
– If you pay like that, the trouble for you will be even greater.Now that he knows in his heart that he has repented, his sins are eliminated. If he wants to repay the debt to the factory, he can "take credit for his sins", try to do a lot of work to contribute to the factory to make up for it, and at the same time explain to his friends so that they can avoid this bad thing, so that they will no longer be greedy to take over national assets as their own.He must use his body as an example and maintain noble and pure conduct.This is knowing how to admit mistakes and repent. Once you know it, you must practice it. You can definitely use merit to make up for past mistakes.

Upon leaving, Mr. Hong respectfully received the Buddhist books, reverently telling the Venerable:
– Please observe me from now on. If I fail to repent, I will have failed your compassion!

Half a month later, Mr. Hong came to my home; stepping through the door, he immediately prostrated before the Buddha altar in the hall. After standing up, he lifted his clothes for me to see, showing off the belt that was no longer there.

He happily said:
– Since that day when I got home, I felt like my illness was more than half healed.I have complied with everything the Venerable Master requested.I built a Buddha altar and a bookcase, and invited the Avalokiteshvara statue to come home early and evening to burn incense and worship.Every day I read the sutras, the Buddhist teachings are really good.Up to now, I have peace of mind, peace of mind, and my illness has healed.These days, our family is as happy as Tet. We are truly grateful to the Venerable.

After I heard it, my heart was filled with joy along with him.Brother Hong is truly "putting down the butcher's knife and immediately becoming a Buddha" like that!

COMMENTS:
The story WHAT'S IN THE WORKSHOP, WHAT'S IN MY HOUSE is a practical lesson about "Greed and theft of public property - the retribution of constant back pain".Mr. Hong took iron, nails, screws, pliers, screwdrivers...from the factory to home to make tools, and "put weight on his back" to the point that he had to wear protective tires for 10 years.When he sincerely repented, vowed never to steal again, established a Buddhist altar at home, and dedicated his diligent labor to the factory to atone for past faults, his ailment was cured. The story emphasizes: "If you want others not to know, it's better to not do it yourself."Even if it's "unwritten" in the office or factory, taking state property home is still theft, and retribution will come on the body.This is a warning to those who are "gentle" with public assets: sooner or later, they must be repaid, and the best way is to repent, practice and make up for it with merit.

tom_tat: Mr. Cao, a former navy veteran, had a brain tumor and had to have his head drilled many times due to killing fish by nailing them to the head and gutting them while they were still alive.Gặp Hòa thượng, sám hối, ăn chay niệm Phật nhưng nghiệp nặng nên giảm thọ.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**PULLING THE HOLE TO REMOVE BAIL**}

Mr. Cao is over 40 years old.Robust personality, working as a security guard at a large company.Three years ago, because I had a headache, I went to the hospital for a check-up and discovered that I had a brain tumor pressing on a nerve, leading to headaches.So the doctor made a hole in his head to remove the pimple.Two years later, he discovered a large cyst in his head and had to have surgery again.This year, the doctor examined me and said that at the same spot where I had the previous puncture, an even larger wart had grown.The doctor said that this time he could not stab his head again, because doing so would endanger his life.

Faced with this difficult situation, he immediately went to ask Venerable Dieu Phap for advice.

The Venerable said:
– Did you work at sea before?He has killed many turtles, and also caught many large live fish, nailed them on boards, then scaled and gutted them.
Mr. Cao was startled when he heard that
– Yes, that's right, I was in the Navy for three years, living on the ocean for a long time.Every day they catch fish to eat.The sea is deep so the fish are especially big, some are over a meter long. The fish is so big that it struggles so much, I immediately use a big nail to stick its head on the board, then start scaling and gutting it.Master, how can you see through such a talented person's entire past?

The monk slowly replied:
– Because, in the past, he drove a nail into a fish's head, so now when he gets sick, he has to scratch his head to treat it.The live fish was nailed to the board and struggled in pain. It was still alive and he was scaling it, gutting it, and removing its internal organs...That scene was extremely cruel.So retribution also came to him each time, one by one.I'm afraid that you didn't just have to drill two or three holes in your head. If you died immediately, it wouldn't be scary at all.What's scary is having to be constantly tormented in pain all year long in a hospital bed, living no better than dying, not being able to achieve good things in general.

The Venerable's words were like thunder, shaking him awake from his coma.

Mr. Cao urgently
– Master, you have great supernatural powers, please save me.

Master gently said:
- "Bodhisattvas fear the cause, sentient beings fear the effect."Now it is time to pay for the sins of the past, you are the one who has to fix them.As long as you sincerely repent, vow to cease killing forever, adopt a pure vegetarian diet, and practice abundant Buddha-recitation, your past faults can be redeemed.

Mr. Cao began that very day to pay homage to the Buddha, chant the Ksitigarbha Sutra, and establish memorial plaques at the temple to pray for the liberation of the creatures he had killed. Until more than two years after his death, he always chanted Buddhist scriptures.He was no longer tormented by suffering.It's just a pity that he passed away when he was less than 50 years old.

Chanting sutras and worshiping the Buddha certainly alleviated his agonizing torment, but because his killing karma was so grave, his lifespan was curtailed. Even though Buddha's power is great, it cannot overcome the karma of sentient beings.Therefore, only by sincerely repenting, vowing to cut off the karma of killing, not eating salty and foul-smelling foods, and preventing people from committing sins is the basis for praying for blessings and longevity.

COMMENTS:
The story of PULLING A HOLE TO GET A BOIL is horrifying proof of "What goes around comes around" in the killing profession.Mr. Cao once drove nails into the heads of live fish and gutted them when they struggled - cruel behavior - so as a result, he had to drill his head many times to remove the brain tumor.Although he subsequently repented, ate vegetarian food, chanted the Ksitigarbha Sutra, and recited the Buddha's name, his heavy killing karma still shortened his lifespan, passing away before age fifty. The story reminds: "Bodhisattvas fear the cause, sentient beings fear the effect."Once karma has been sown, even if you practice, it will only reduce the suffering but cannot erase it.People who are engaged in fishing and slaughtering should soon wake up and stop killing to avoid tragic retribution on their own bodies.

tom_tat: A Taiwanese rich woman has sinusitis due to her habit of chewing bones and sucking fish marrow after cooking for her mother-in-law and children.Meeting Venerable Dieu Phap, being taught about the sins of killing and eating organs, repenting and recovering from illness.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**CHEW THE BONES WITH THE SPOT OF THE Marrow**}

In the summer of 1996, a rich man's wife arrived from Taiwan.She had been suffering from sinusitis for more than ten years and had not recovered, so she had to go to Mainland, to Ngu Dai Mountain to pay her respects to the Venerable.Pray for Him to point out the cause of the disease.

Teacher asked:
– When you got married, your husband's family situation was not very good?
– Yes, that's right!– She said

– After marriage, with so many children born, our family situation worsened steadily, and life became terribly difficult and impoverished...
– Yes, that's right!

– Sometimes she goes to the market to buy a few fish, and after cooking, she always brings the best dish to her mother-in-law.The fish's body and tail are also divided for the children to eat.The remaining fish head bone she could not bear to throw away.You should put it in your mouth, chew it and suck its pulp.Later, even though her family was rich, her old habits were deeply rooted and kept recurring.Until now, when you eat fish, you still like to chew its bones and swallow its marrow, right?

– That's right, Master.Because it has become a habit, I find fish bones delicious to eat.But what you eat when you are awake is the three pure flesh (meat is among the three things: Eyes do not see the person killing, ears do not hear the person killing, it is not killing for yourself to eat) right?Isn't it allowed to eat?– There's something you don't understand, so ask again.

– Eating the three pure flesh is a way of teaching the Dharma for beginners to Buddhism.Because if you tell people to stop eating salty foods right away, I'm afraid many people won't be able to do it.That's why we ask them not to kill.Eating the three pure flesh - It is just the Buddha's way of guiding sentient beings - Depending on their diligent efforts to constantly recite Buddha's name and chant sutras, they naturally no longer think about eating salty food.Ultimately, eating meat is killing!You need to quickly eliminate and strictly observe the precepts of killing to be correct - Master explained.

– Master, is it a sin to eat fish bones and fish heads?– She still doesn't understand, so ask again

– Flesh and bones – These are all parts of an animal's body, and we often use the words "pulling tendons, peeling skin, chewing bones, swallowing marrow", saying that to also visualize and describe the mood of an angry person.We must know that animals are being killed by us.The heart is filled with fear at the approach of death and towards the person who kills it, as well as great hatred for the person who devours it.Because all sentient beings, usually everyone, is attached to their body, loves their body very much, thinks that the flesh body that is eaten is theirs, so even when they die, their consciousness absolutely refuses to leave the body, regardless of whether the person's body is chopped up, swallowed alive, or cooked such as roasting, grilling, stir-frying...Only the enlightened ones and those who practice do not cling to the body, while those who practice poorly have high attachment and much anger.Therefore, even though it is dead, when the animal's consciousness sees its body being chopped up, cooked, chewed and swallowed, it still feels extremely painful and painful...Therefore, when a meat eater pulls out the tendons and peels the animal's skin, chews the bones and swallows the marrow, or even brutally slaughters an animal, doesn't he just swing his knife to finish it off?But the suffering inflicted on the animal continues to increase, so its resentment towards me is very deep.Because of this reason, she had to bring illness into her body, the illnesses piled up, and she often encountered unsatisfactory situations.

Therefore, Buddhist practitioners and believers should not consume even the three types of purified meat, and even less should they eat animal internal organs such as heart, liver, lungs, eyes, tongue, brain, and marrow... Don't be foolish enough to believe that whatever you eat is nutritious, don't think that eating like that has great nutritional benefits.You don't know that the more internal organs you eat, the deeper your hatred towards animals will be.Over time, many dangerous diseases develop in the internal organs of the body.

– Master, that's so scary!So can my child's sinusitis be cured?

– On the condition that she must sincerely repent, vow to completely stop eating salty food, do many good deeds and release many animals.

– If every day you can recite a set of Ksitigarbha Sutra and dedicate it to sentient beings in the dharma world, you will definitely receive good results.When releasing animals, they must be released somewhere where the fish can easily live. They should not be released into a fish farmer's pond to wait for them to be eaten.It should be released into rivers, seas, large ponds and lakes, so that it can truly reproduce.The same goes for all kinds of birds and wild animals, let them go somewhere safe for them.If the economy is good, you can release turtles and many other animals, there will be even more great merit, making up for the mistakes of killing in the past.They all have spirits, perhaps in this life they can also repay her kindness. We often see these returns.Done, do you now have enough faith to keep the precepts - Never kill and never eat salty food?

- Yes, when I return, I will definitely follow your instructions - She said firmly

Chewing bones and swallowing marrow can cause illness, this is natural.This time, I listened to Master explain in detail, so I was deeply impressed.So carefully recorded it.We hope that Dharma travelers will pay attention and be careful to reap benefits together.

As for the rich lady in Taiwan, later her rhinitis was completely cured. She even returned to Wutai Mountain to express her gratitude and earnestly bow to the Venerable.

COMMENTS:
The story of CHEWING BONES WITH MULLETS is a profound lesson about "Eating animal organs - causing disease in the corresponding organ".The rich man's habit of chewing bones and sucking fish marrow (even if it was "three pure flesh") caused constant sinusitis.Venerable Dieu Phap clearly explained: when the animal is killed, the consciousness still clings to the body, seeing its body being chewed and swallowed, it causes deep resentment.The more internal organs you eat, the deeper your resentment and the more serious the illness in the corresponding organ.After repenting, vowing to stop eating salty food, chanting the Ksitigarbha Sutra and releasing animals, the disease was completely cured.A cautionary tale: "What you eat is nutritious" is a misconception and dangerous.Animal organs are not a tonic, but a "debt" waiting to be claimed.People like to eat heart, liver, lungs, marrow, eyes...Please wake up soon to avoid retribution.

tieu_de: 10. LAY PRACTITIONERS MUST ALSO CULTIVATE VIRTUE
tom_tat: Anh thợ họ Lý quy y Phật, đi chùa công quả nhưng lấy cúng phẩm về nhà chia cho vợ con, ngồi thiền đòi người khác hầu hạ. His wife came to argue and was explained about the virtues of lay people.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**LAYERS MUST ALSO HAVE ENOUGH VIRTUES**}

In 1993, a tailor named Li came to my house to hear the Master lecture on the Dharma, and he developed faith in Buddhism. Half a month later he asked for refuge in the Three Jewels, and even brought the "refuge certificate" to show it to me.

From then on, every Sunday on his day off, he went to the temple to volunteer, offering service as a security guard to maintain order during Dharma assemblies.

Half a month later, while discussing the Dharma with friends at home, Brother Li and his wife visited. After greeting us, they sat aside listening to our conversation.

Waiting for us to finish talking, Mr. Ly's wife confided:
– Today I originally wanted to find my brother to reason with me.But just now I heard the words my brother said to everyone, they were all about guiding and guiding them towards goodness.Last month, when my husband stopped by my brother's house, he came home and said, "I want to become a layman."Half a month later, he took refuge in Buddha and became a layman...

She paused for a moment and then said with a warm expression:
– But I don't understand what is called a "lay person"?I thought my husband learned some good things or did something good for me.To my surprise, from that day on, every Sunday he went to the temple, saying he was volunteering and protecting the Dharma... At night, bring fruit, incense, oil...home, saying that nowadays many people believe in Buddhism and offerings are boundless—oil, incense, fruit, cakes... anything.Where can the monks eat everything?So when lay people come to merit, they must share it.I heard that and it's no different from him making money, so why is he still showing off his merits of protecting the dharma for the temple?I think that doesn't seem reasonable at all?What's even more ridiculous is that every day when he gets home from work, he keeps crossing his thighs and showing off that he's sitting quietly...But every little bit he asked me to bring him water, every little bit he asked me for food.I said "I'm busy cooking, please serve yourself"...Then he said I had trouble sitting, my thighs couldn't let go!It's really frustrating, being a "lay person" like that is not doing...What about someone's father?Or has he been ordained and become a high-ranking figure of some level?If that's true, then I also want to be a lay person and practice meditating like him. Let's see who serves who?Today I'm so angry that I'm here to argue with you!

She spoke in one breath, making me extremely shocked.It turns out that the story I heard about "Lay Buddhists fighting over the distribution of offerings in the temple" is true?Just heard it with my own ears today, it's clear evidence of reality.I even heard that fights broke out because of the uneven distribution of offerings?

I once looked at the sutra and saw it written like this: "A grain of rice that the donor is as heavy as Mount Meru, if he eats it without cultivating, he must wear feathers and horns to repay it."

How then could a layperson take home offerings made by devotees to the Triple Gem, intended to support monastics and sustain the Dharma? There was also a fight and a fight, this is a very sinful thing!

If a monastic person receives offerings from the ten directions, if he does not practice properly, he will fall into the evil path, let alone a lay person?Not only will it be difficult to fall into hell in the future, but the blessings you have in this life can also be lost!Let me give an example: If the Venerable's conduct is pure, then his happiness is like a good, fertile land.When they come to make offerings from the ten good directions, it is to sow blessings on that land.The land will definitely reward those who cultivate diligently.

If the Venerable's conduct is not strict, it will be like bad and dry land, unable to give people a good harvest.Even their own harvest was encroached by wild grass, and in the end it was difficult to avoid crop failure.

Furthermore, as laypersons whose field of merit cannot match that of the monastic Sangha, how could we bring foul habits of greed, anger, and delusion to defile the pure gates of the temple?

Venerable Dieu Phap once said: "If the Vietnamese monks offer food, but the monks cannot eat it all and it is not convenient to store it, it can be distributed to lay people to take home, but must be approved by the Abbot.And when lay people receive gifts and want to save blessings, they can base on the approximate value of the item they are holding and put money into the blessing box to create more merit.Or people who do meritorious deeds can also take them to the market and sell them, bringing the money back to the pagoda. This is also the right dharma, knowing how to accumulate merit, knowing how to fear losing blessings.Protecting the pagoda is inherently the duty of lay people, so how can you use that as an excuse to plunder wealth?Do you still feel greedy and fight with each other?This ignorant behavior only makes Buddhism more negatively affected.

On this occasion, I urgently request my fellow lay followers, after finishing work, to take the time to recite the Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva Sutra and the Luong Hoang Sam Sutra. Let us recite with sincerity and earnestness. We will definitely generate great and noble minds, destroy all obstacles, and gain immeasurable blessings.

The purpose of studying Buddhism is to gain wisdom and gain enlightenment.Wash away the three poisons, greed, anger, and delusion that have been contaminated for a long time in the five impurities of life from beginningless kalpas to the present.Once wise persons recognize that their bad habits are the very causes casting them into the three evil paths (hells, hungry ghosts, animals), how could they knowingly continue to commit wrongdoings? If you immerse yourself in the abyss, it will be difficult for you to emerge?

When lay people come to the temple, they must study Buddhism in order to "penetrate the sutras and gain wisdom like the ocean." They must always study and practice according to Buddhist practices.Only when true wisdom is unfolded can we deeply believe in karmic cause and effect and walk vigilantly, deeply moved by the selfless compassion of the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Sangha.

Buddha never covers and tolerates people who have the "Refuge Sect" or punishes anyone who does not have the "Refuge Sect".

The Buddha always proclaimed the truth with boundless compassionate concern, hoping all people might awaken from delusion, return to righteousness, and leave suffering to attain happiness.

But the path in human life must be walked by ourselves.Understanding this clearly, we lay practitioners must cultivate virtue and accumulate blessings, coming to temples with a humble, reforming mind to support the Dharma and Sangha, sincerely studying teachings to fulfill both self-benefit and the benefit of others.

COMMENTS:
The story of LAYERS SHOULD HAVE ENOUGH VIRTUES is a stern warning to lay people who are "nothing but real".Brother Li took refuge and volunteered at temples, yet took offerings home for his family and demanded his wife wait upon him while meditating—such conduct was greedy and arrogant, completely contrary to the Buddhist spirit of benefiting self and others. His wife asked the question on our behalf: “What is a lay person?Is it to be served and take back offerings?”The answer is: Lay people must have enough virtue, know how to save blessings, know shame, and practice honestly.Accepting offerings must have the abbot's permission and you should put money in the blessing box to create merit.The story reminds: "A benefactor's grain of rice is as heavy as Mount Meru, if he eats it without cultivating, he must wear feathers and horns to repay it."People with the title of lay people should examine their own minds and not let the "pure Buddha door" become a place to nurture bad habits.

tieu_de: 11. THE ANT NEST AND THE HOUSE
tom_tat: The family destroyed the ant nest for many years, causing them to be unable to find stable housing for 3 years.Meeting Venerable Dieu Phap, the cause and effect was clearly shown, repentance and chanting sutras dedicated to the ants.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**ESTATE AND HOUSING**}

A couple brought their son, about ten years old, to ask to see Venerable Dieu Phap to ask for advice.

Three years ago, they moved from Taiwan to settle abroad.First, they temporarily rented a room to stay, and planned to later choose to buy a suitable villa to live in.

But buying a house is difficult because the family of four always disagrees. Whenever the husband likes it, the wife doesn't agree, or vice versa.Or if you like it, your parents won't agree.It's not easy to find a house where all four people are satisfied.But when the whole family agrees, there's a reason the homeowner doesn't want to sell.Just like that, this process lasted for nearly three years.Up to now, they have not been able to find a suitable house to buy, which makes them think forever without understanding why.

Because the couple held deep faith in the Buddha, they began to doubt their own blessings, wondering if their merit was deficient. During their vacation, they traveled to Mount Wutai to pay homage to the Buddha and request Venerable Miao Fa to resolve their doubts.

Listening to their stories, Master just smiled and gently asked his two sons:
– You two mischievous children, do you like to disturb the ant nest or not?
Hearing Master's question, the entire family of four burst into laughter.

The mother said:
– Yes, when we were children, we really liked to destroy ant nests. We said we wanted to study the structure of the ant nest. We also praised the nest's very good design. There was a palace for the queen ant, a majestic barracks for the worker ants, and a lot of food in storage...Yes, the two of us were so engrossed in studying and playing that we even forgot to eat and drink...

Master said:
– These two children love to destroy ant nests, destroy many houses that the ants have created through countless hardships, and also destroy and destroy the food that the ants have been gathering for many years everywhere. Their actions have caused them to lose a place to live and rest.

For that reason, today you are not at peace wherever you are, and you can't find a home!This is just a preliminary warning. If you do not know how to repent and correct your mistakes, in the future when you have a house, your house will be unexpectedly destroyed.No matter how rich your children are, in the future it will be difficult to escape the situation of sometimes having to struggle to find food.

Turning to the two adults, the Venerable scolded:
– And the two of you as parents, having taken refuge for many years, how could you stand by idly and let your children perform such destructive acts without admonishing and guiding them? "Raising without teaching is the parents' fault." Children must know that cause and effect is like a shadow following a shape.If you repent early, create blessings, and diligently chant sutras to dedicate merit to the thousands of ants whose lives and property you have damaged, then perhaps future disasters will be changed.Got it?

After receiving the Venerable's explanation, the couple was moved by repentance and said:
– Master, we acknowledge our faults. Although we took refuge years ago, we assumed that observing a vegetarian diet and reciting the Buddha's name was already sufficient! I didn't expect it to be this serious.After we return, our whole family will repent before the Buddha, reciting the Ksitigarbha Sutra and Great Compassion Mantra to dedicate merits to the ants. Would that be acceptable?

– How good, how good!Very well, always remember deeply: 'All sentient beings possess the potential to attain Buddhahood.' Therefore, never despise animals, and never arbitrarily harm living beings! – Teacher earnestly reminded.

COMMENTS:
The story NEST AND HOUSING is a vivid lesson about "Destroying the homes of living beings - the retribution of not having a stable home".The two children destroyed the ant nest and were passionate about "research", their parents did not stop them - that was the cause.The retribution was not being able to buy a house for 3 years, the family was in discord, and everyone was not satisfied.Venerable Dieu Phap pointed out: "Raising without teaching is the parents' fault."After the whole family repented and chanted sutras to dedicate to the ants, it was hoped that cause and effect would be transformed.The story reminds: All sentient beings have the ability to become Buddhas, do not underestimate small animals.Destroying ant nests, burning beehives, or harming animals' homes is also creating karma, and the retribution will come in the form of "no safe place" for yourself and your descendants.

tieu_de: 12. EXPECTANT MOTHERS RECITING THE KSITIGARBHA SUTRA
tom_tat: Hai Ba is 7 months pregnant, the fetus often kicks painfully.Advised to recite the Ksitigarbha Sutra, eat a vegetarian diet, give birth smoothly, the baby is healthy and does not cry when drinking milk containing salty foods.
noi_dung:
{align:center|**PREGNANT WOMEN RETURN TO THE Ksitigarbha Meridian**}

Four years ago I met a girl named Hai Ba, a student, calm, beautiful, and very intelligent.She is originally from the Northeast and was born into a family that believes in Buddhism.

At the beginning of this year, Hai Ba was seven months pregnant. She told me that the baby in her belly kept kicking around, causing her pain, and asked me if there was anything I could do to help her?

I told her to recite one Ksitigarbha sutra every day, continuously for 7 days, which could not only help eliminate karma from previous lives, but also help stabilize the unjust fate between mother and child in previous lives.In addition, doing this will make it easier for her to give birth, without suffering, and the child born will also be peaceful and easy to raise.Even if you get sick sometimes, you will be healthy.If she could start being a vegetarian now, it would be even better!

Hai Ba asked me again if chicken eggs can be eaten?I said the market today specializes in raising egg-laying chickens.If the egg is not empty, you can eat it.

Two months later, Hai Ba called to thank me and boasted that he had just returned home from the maternity hospital.All are favorable.She also happily informed me that when I asked her to recite seven sets of the Ksitigarbha Sutra, in her heart she silently vowed to recite 49 sets.Fortunately, as soon as she finished chanting the 49 sets, she was admitted to the hospital and gave birth the next day. At the time of giving birth, the doctor asked her to try harder. At that time, she wanted to chant the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, but as soon as she thought so, she heard the doctor say: - You see the baby's head.

When the doctor told her that the baby boy was born healthy and chubby, she cried with joy.She stayed in the hospital for four days and saw that other pregnant women had to give birth by cesarean section, and she was the only one who had an easy birth.

The reason is because the hospital's income is increasing, and pregnant women want to have a smooth birth and let the doctor perform a cesarean section.But everyone understands that a cesarean section both hurts the body and wastes resources.It's really just the force of karma that attracts me.

Ten days later, Hai Ba called to tell him that the day he came home from the hospital, the baby didn't cry even a bit.But three days later, she cried again, continuously for a week, and cried while breastfeeding.No matter what.The baby also has a fever, I don't know what is the cause?

I asked:
– Do you eat any other food?
She explained that her mother-in-law came from the countryside and saw that she was a vegetarian and did not eat meat, so she was very angry.She insisted that she eat herring to nourish her body.So she had to reluctantly eat to make her happy.Then she lamented:
– Your mother-in-law wants to kill a stewed hen for me to eat.What to do now?

I said:
- The reason why the child is crying loudly is because since you recited the 49 Ksitigarbha Sutras for him, he has eliminated his karma and increased his wisdom.So it doesn't want to drink milk that contains salty foods.If she didn't eat meat and fish, the baby certainly wouldn't cry.
